title: VeinSqueeze, two separate readings of one scan
caption: One part reads 32 ultrasound frames and gives a clot chance; a separate part outlines the vein in every frame to show how far it squeezes, and never feeds the clot chance.
alt: Architecture diagram of VeinSqueeze in two panels that never connect. Panel (a), the clot classifier with 9.9 million parameters, the AI second opinion: 32 grey ultrasound frames of 160 by 160 pixels are normalised and each frame passes a MobileNetV4 Conv-Medium encoder, giving 1280 numbers per frame; a linear layer maps these to 256 and adds the frame position; two transformer blocks with 4 heads look across the 32 frames; then a LayerNorm, gated attention pooling with one weight per frame, and linear heads give the clot chance (2.2 percent on the shown clip) and a guess of the vein site (great saphenous). Panel (b), the squeeze curve, an explanation only that never feeds the clot chance: the same clip, every frame, with two clicks (a plus on the vein, a minus on the artery), goes into SAM 2.1-large, used zero-shot with 224 million parameters, which outlines the vein in all 98 frames; four example frames show the outline at 101, 59, 16 and 85 percent of the starting area. The area is divided by the starting area (the median of frames 0 to 4) and smoothed with a 5-frame median, giving the squeeze curve over 3 seconds: it falls from about 100 percent to a lowest point of 16 percent at 1.35 seconds, in the partly closed band, then rises again. Bands are our own rule: 10 percent or less closed fully, 10 to 50 percent partly closed, above 50 percent stayed open. Images: held-out clip D from the ThrombUS+ dataset (CC BY 4.0).
